definition: Reproducible Model Training is a core concept in AI Engineering. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Reproducible Model Training is
theory.body: Reproducible Model Training describes the methods and patterns used within AI Engineering to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Reproducible Model Training is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Reproducible Model Training matters
theory.body: Without Reproducible Model Training, systems built with AI Engineering are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Reproducible Model Training works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Reproducible Model Training follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Reproducible Model Training.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Reproducible Model Training
theory.body: Reproducible Model Training offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
